feedback: Color for each category is good, glyph is also nice to make the titles pop. Second line for a deferred message means that these are going to take a lot of vertical space, especially because many of these lines you've printed are mostly empty.  The last one takeing 3 lines is really a lot, and depending on which and how many messages are displayed, 3 lines is really a lot of display space.
title: Deferred notices as prefixed lines, ltl look

feedback: Yeah, I still like the color, the bar isn't a bad idea.  I don't like however that the category name is printed multiple times within the same category.  Category notices should be brgrouped together and only print the category name once.  You have to think about wasted characters, and reprinting the same thing over and over is hard for a reader to process.  Things need to present information simply, with a minimum explanation and detail to understand and know what to do.
title: Deferred notices as prefixed lines, new style

feedback: Yes, boxed method like this was more what I had in mind showing that this is the notice surface.  I like this per category approach if only a single category is being printed, however if there are multiples, I feel like the lines could be too busy.  It would be good to have an alternative option to this one which has a boxed section for the notices overall, then inside of that, lines or empty CR divides them.
title: One box per category, ltl look

feedback: Yeah, I like it.  Similar to my last feedback, the per category outline is nice if there are only 1-2, but starts to be a lot if there are very many to display.  First option feedback still holds here as well as the Data anomaly section with 2 notices takes 6 lines inside the box, with 2 more for the box, that is 8 verticle lines for 2 notifications which is a lot.
title: One box per category, new style

feedback: Yes, I like it.  Using case to help make the category title jump out and be differentiated from the notice/message text is good.  I also really like that this line contains other useful information like explaining what the category is for, this is really helpful for a user to adapt their own context around how they should be reading messages in each category/section.
title: Headed sections, ltl look

feedback: This is cleaner than your previous variant like this where the larger vertical bars were used on each line.  I like the space between each category, this makes it much more readible, however it also means that the overall notice surface printing takes up a lot more lines.  I'm not sure that I like the thinner lines compared to the wider ones.  Overall there is still the problem that the horizontal data density is quite low (right side mostly empty), and vertical density is taking up half of the terminal window only for notices.
title: Headed sections, new style

feedback: This is wasteful, it shouldn't be 2 lines for the single notice.  This is hardly minimal.
title: A single deprecation, the smallest surface

feedback: Eek.  This is horrible.  Space after the emoji and before the category name is not consistent.  DATA ANOMALY as no space at all, same with YOUR OPTIONS.  DECISION TAKEN FOR YOU and FIGURE CAVEAT are fine.  GUIDANCE has way too much space.  I also can't say that these emojis are very relevant to what each category positions/states.
title: Headed sections with emoji glyphs

feedback: Beh.  This is pointless.  I likely the character glyphs, but here the ASCII characters seem to be trying to do something which is pointless and they don't bring any value beyond the category name.
title: Headed sections with ASCII marks

feedback: Hitting a key other than one of the choices should stop the countdown, allowing the user the time to read and think.  The layout here doesn't really make much sense to me, but the choice line is fine.
title: Option notices, then a timed question below them

feedback: I like the bolded or bright white for the choices.  It helps make pop what needs to be chosen.  Same other feedback as to the last option.
title: Option notices as a section, question below, new style

feedback: This is just weird with the box not completely drawn.  If you could draw the bottom of the box and then come back up to the previous line for the choice this might make more sense, but as is this is useless and just looks bad.
title: Notices and question in one frame, ltl look

feedback: This is the same as previous feedback.
title: Notices and question in one frame, new style

feedback: Too much lost horizontal space.  text only uses the left 2/3rds of the terminal which then takes many lines with most of the space being empty.  IIf we could do cursor position across the display surface, this is the sort of message that would possibly work better as a modal window if it could be earsaed afterwards.  Otherwise, the minimal nature of this option is good, but still, like I've said before, this takes too many lines, you should not have any carriage returns in this notice.  You are already using 3 colors, and a special arrow character which visually split up the parts of the notice quite nicely so vertial spacing is not needed.
title: Question over the progress line: notice above, stays

feedback: Yeah... that good.  a tiny bit of detail is lacking, likely with the color differences, notice sections, etc. then this would be perfect; essentially mixing the previous case with this one to get it all on a single line.
title: Question in the progress row itself

feedback: Yes, love that one.  For most minimal, the last one with suggested variation takes it.  For more detail, this one takes it (still noting that the 3 lines for the message is excessive)
title: Boxed notice over the progress line, ltl look

feedback: Yes, I like this one too.  Frankly, I like the color of the box here.  This is a place that the new style with colored box edge makes sense as there is a single box displayed and then removed, so it brings the focus into the box while the choice is taken, and then the box disappears, so that it doesn't take up screen space and cause visual load once the choice that it served was taken.
title: Boxed notice over the progress line, new style

feedback:
For all of the other categories, there are different parts of the notice, using different colors, and even some glyphs as seperators.  Here in the guidance section this is missing and required.  The parts should be separated; there is the focus area (POST .../QueryStreamEntriesWithData), then there is the automated analysis.
Two second choice is too short, and similar as to said before, any other key should stop the countdown to the automatic choice.
The second stage then is a nice list, but it is horribly out of place as you've put the first stage in a boxed section, yet the second selection is not.  It should be a consistent progression.  In this example, the guidance is one message, so perhaps earsing the initial choice and the bottom of the GUIDANCE box, then enlarging the box, and including the list inside the box while the user is selecting the option for the second stage.
title: Two-stage choice, vertical list, ltl look

feedback: Same feedback as before, this is just a different box color.
title: Two-stage choice, vertical list, new style

feedback: This is certainly more minimalistic, which would as fallback on a very small terminal, or if some reason the boxes couldn't be drawn, however overall I'm not impressed.  Even with the bullet glyph for the choice, the second stage selection is very simplistic with the numbers.  Also, whats missing is the explanation that the navigable list has.  This could be good if the terminal can't pickup the arrow keys however.
title: Two-stage choice, one row chosen by a digit

feedback: Eek.  So here upon refusal, this should erase the choice all together like the during processing one does, this way the prompt only stays present while asking the question, then once answered it is all gone and doesn't take up display space when it was refused.  Along those lines, you example here has redundant output, once when the selection says continue as planned, and then you have the next line stating continue as planned.  This is not coherent, is wasteful, and adds nothing at all.
title: Two-stage choice, declined at stage one

feedback: I really like this option when the noticed to navigate and explore are long and data is dense.  This is a really good way to handle the density of all of the notices and each of their parts, allowing the analyst to go over them.  However here it is shown as if it is inline, and I think that this display mode would really be better surrounded by a box where the contents are shown over top of other things, and then upon closing it out it would be erased/removed.  This would also need to be combined with the various other multi-stage options, so that for example we could come back to this main notice navigator after having made the selections for one of the two-stage selections as far as what to do next.
title: Inline list of 25 notices with a detail pane, ltl look

feedback: I like this one a lot just as the last one for displaying and navigating a long list of notificdations.  However I don't see how this 'new' style is any different from the 'ltl' style.
title: Inline list with a detail pane, new style

feedback: So the full screen view is way, way overkill.  However, I do like the tabbed navigation if you are at the top level and navigate right or left to essentially filter notices to the selected category.  That could be handy.  I could also imagine using the number keys to select the first, second, third, etc tab to provide alternative navigation from the arrow keys.  I should also say that j and k should be allowed for fallback navigation for less capable terminals.
title: Full-screen list with category tabs, ltl look

feedback: Same feedback from last scenario.
title: Full-screen list with category tabs, new style

feedback: Yeah, this one is really nice.  It takes up a lot of space, but immediately brings focus to the user about the question, which is the point of such a modal pop-up.  The fact that it erases itself after the choice is taken means that the extra vertical space used to bring clarity to the presentation isn't a cost for excessive visual and cognitive load by adding too much information to the screen as it is done piece by piece and is only relevant to the context in question.
title: Modal during the read, drawn below the cursor

feedback: Yeah, I mean this one actually fits my feedback from the previous scenario better.  the key is to make it front and center, get the attention, get the choice, and then go back to the normal execution, so this is likely better than the whole same screen with additional lines printed.  Perhaps this one is the primary approach, and the other one is the fallback.
title: Modal during the read, on the alternate screen

feedback: I mean, we need to standardize on approaches, so your framing that we'd have a different way of displaying things and asking for user input in each of these scenarios is wrong.  We are looking for a standard set of patterns and approaches which we then commit to and they then become the standards for all relevant usage and call on them as is guided by our design decisions and shared libraries that we pout in place
title: Modal once a pattern is found, below the cursor, new style

feedback: Yeah, I like the previous one better in this case, but it doesn't really matter.  In any case, I think that the last scenario is the fallback, and then perhaps the usage pattern passes in the preference of alternative screen or same screen.
title: Modal once a pattern is found, alternate screen, new style
